paper_excerpts.Original first sentence: This insight applies when the problem domain requires resources to move or transform through nodes and local conservation must hold.
paper_excerpts.Added applicability clause: This insight applies when the optimization model includes explicit resource-budget or capacity limits that must be enforced through conservation-style inequalities, especially for a coupled routing-and-service problem where vehicles, payload, service time, battery charge, or facility throughput are consumed along routes.

paper_excerpts.Original condition: This insight applies when a binary decision should switch a continuous quantity on or off.
paper_excerpts.Added applicability clause: This insight applies when the model explicitly has a continuous service quantity whose existence depends on a binary activation variable, such as served demand, flow, or capacity being present only if a route, link, or facility is opened.
paper_excerpts.Exclusion excerpt: the problem is a discrete facility-location/assignment model with binary build, served/not-served, and routing/allocation decisions rather than a continuous quantity that must be switched on or off

paper_excerpts.Original condition: This insight applies when a binary open/closed decision should activate or deactivate route use.
paper_excerpts.Added applicability clause: This insight applies when the model contains a facility-opening binary that is supposed to condition actual route, departure, return, or traversal arcs, such as depot/station/vertiport opening variables linked to drone, vehicle, or flow routes.
paper_excerpts.Added exclusion clause: This insight does NOT apply when the decision problem is a facility siting, coverage, or assignment model without route-arc decisions that must be switched on/off by facility-opening binaries.

paper_excerpts.Before: This insight applies when a binary open/closed decision should activate or deactivate route use.
paper_excerpts.After: This insight applies when two cues appear together: a binary open/closed site variable and an arc-activation or route-permission rule.
